question: Does moderate additional MEL/BKL training exposure improve a proven ConvNeXt checkpoint and its fixed ensemble over a matched warm-start control?
loss: training-only sqrt weighted cross entropy; full effective-batch weight denominator
targeted_sampling: All train indices plus one additional copy of each MEL/BKL training index; shuffle, trim terminal batch to effective32. No DF/VASC repetition; no validation-derived sample weights.
control_sampling: All train indices plus the same number of extra uniformly drawn training indices, without replacement within extras; same epoch draw count and optimizer-update budget as targeted arm.
optimizer: fresh AdamW for both arms, not an exact continuation of source optimizer
training_precision: FP16 AMP GradScaler as proven strict recipe
scheduler: ReduceLROnPlateau factor.5 patience1 meaningful threshold.002 minlr1e-7; identical arms
pilot_gate: Selected fixed ensemble must beat both original and matched control by >=.005 accuracy, maintain macroF1, improve mean MEL/BKL recall >=.02, neither focus recall lower by >.01, NV recall lower by <=.01
late_gate: After10 total targeted epochs require >=.002 selected ensemble accuracy gain over epoch5 pilot plus initial gate
checkpoint_selection: Earliest raw maximum standalone accuracy; parent checkpoint retained as epoch0 if no improvement; independent macroF1 winner
